vehicle_or_wheel: Scarecrow and DTM (Dynamic Test Model, 437 kg, same wheels, 128% of Mars weight of flight rover)
terrain_description: Artificially built cohesionless sand slopes in the JPL Marsyard, 5 m wide by 9 m long track, flat to 20 deg; five DTM trials and three Scarecrow trials
soil_parameters_reported: Well sorted sand, grain size 250 to 425 um; some subsurface moisture detected; cone penetrometer data given only as Figure 8
method: Direct upslope drive, GPS or motion capture ground truth, slip from Eq. 4
metric: Slope at which both vehicles embed in sand (transition from marginal slip)
source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al. 2013, J. Field Robotics 30(6), 835-846)
passage_or_location: Section 6.3, p. 842 text accompanying Figure 11; Abstract, p. 835
comparability_warning: Prepared test bed (counted as lab); moisture caused packing between grousers at high sinkage that true cohesionless sand would not show; sparse points near transition
notes: Text: both vehicles traverse up 10 deg slopes with marginal slip. Marginal slip is not quantified in text. Section 6.3 also states inflection between 10 and 17 deg at Dumont Dunes.

vehicle_or_wheel: Scarecrow (50 cm wheel diameter, EGP 5.75 kPa) vs SSTB-Lite (MER test vehicle, 26.2 cm wheel diameter, EGP 5.72 kPa)
terrain_description: Cohesionless sand, Dumont Dunes, Mojave Desert CA; side by side on same 12 deg slope
soil_parameters_reported: Not reported
method: Direct side by side upslope comparison; SSTB-Lite slip by counting wheel rotations and tape measure, Scarecrow by motion capture
metric: Maximum slope climbed vs embedding (wheel diameter effect at near equal ground pressure)
value: Scarecrow climbed 15 deg slope and ascended 12 deg slope; SSTB-Lite embedded on 12 deg slope
source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al. 2013, J. Field Robotics 30(6), 835-846)
passage_or_location: Section 7, p. 843 to 844, Figure 15 text and Table III p. 839
comparability_warning: Different slip measurement methods for the two vehicles (less accurate for SSTB-Lite); single comparison slope; outcome is binary, no slip value
notes: Ground pressure difference under 1%. Paper attributes the difference to wheel curvature and motion resistance, citing Skonieczny et al. 2012 and Wong 2008.

vehicle_or_wheel: Scarecrow (Mars weight MSL test rover, 340 kg, 50 cm diameter rigid grousered wheels, 40 cm wide, EGP 5.75 kPa) and DTM
terrain_description: Smooth flagstone simulated bedrock (Marsyard, 5 to 30 deg) and cohesive soil (Marsyard and desiccated lake bed at Tecopa CA, flat to 28 deg)
soil_parameters_reported: Not reported numerically; cohesive soil described as variable with moisture, compaction and cohesion; cone penetrometer data only in Figure 8
method: Direct upslope drives, slip vs slope compiled per terrain
metric: Maximum traversable slope; slip at that slope
value: Bedrock up to 22 deg; cohesive soil at Tecopa 28 deg with less than 50% slip (Section 6.2) or 30% slip (Section 10); Marsyard cohesive soil up to 75% slip at 20 deg without embedding
source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al. 2013, J. Field Robotics 30(6), 835-846)
passage_or_location: Abstract p. 835; Section 6.1 p. 841 to 842; Section 6.2 p. 842; Section 10 p. 845
comparability_warning: Bedrock result is lab (constructed flagstone Marsyard track) while Tecopa is field; cohesive soil is highly variable; paper gives two slip figures for 28 deg (under 50% and 30%)
notes: At 30 deg smooth flagstone the rover limit cycled and made no significant upslope progress. Inflection point for textured bedrock expected between 20 and 35 deg (stated as expectation, not measured). Values from text, not plots.

vehicle_or_wheel: Curiosity (MSL, 899 kg, flight rover on Mars) using onboard slip model
terrain_description: Hummocky well consolidated soil at Gale Crater, Mars, first 250 sols, 723 m driven as of 1 May 2013
soil_parameters_reported: Terrain classed as most similar to the cohesive soil in Earth testing; no parameters reported
method: Third order polynomial slip vs slope model, coefficients set by terrain type from terrestrial tests, used to estimate downslope slip from roll and pitch; slip measured on Mars by visual odometry
metric: Agreement of Earth based slip prediction with Mars slip data
value: good agreement (qualitative; no numeric error reported)
source_title: Traverse Performance Characterization for the Mars Science Laboratory Rover (Heverly et al. 2013, J. Field Robotics 30(6), 835-846)
passage_or_location: Abstract p. 835; Section 9 p. 844 to 845 and Figure 17; Section 10 p. 845
comparability_warning: No quantitative prediction error given in text; agreement judged from Figure 17 overlay; limited terrain and slope range on Mars to date
notes: Model coefficients to be adjusted as more Mars data arrive. Meridiani ripple embedding of Opportunity (446th sol, more than five weeks to extricate) is mentioned only qualitatively in Section 1, p. 835; no slip values for Meridiani, Rocknest or sand ripples are in this paper.
